#59438. Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?

Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (976 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In its role as president of negotiations at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Australia is being pressured to guide nations toward unified action on slashing the greenhouse gas emissions that are generated in large part by burning fossil fuels.
  • The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.
  • "Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," said Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In its role as president of negotiations at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Australia is being pressured to guide nations toward unified action on slashing the greenhouse gas emissions that are generated in large part by burning fossil fuels.

The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.

"Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," said Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.

It has been revealed that "These are proven, commercial and scalable today. Now is the moment for faster implementation.".

Yet Australia is also the world's third-largest exporter of fossil fuels. And unlike France and Germany, or island nations from Fiji to the Bahamas that are highly vulnerable to a changing climate, the COP31 co-president has not yet committed to phasing them out.

As calls grow for the country to set a clear route to a clean energy future, critics say its vague promise to transition away from polluting sources of power does not go far enough.

Australia is home to 56% of the world's coal mine projects currently in the pipeline, notes environmental nonprofit, 350.org.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at the organization, is calling on the country, the world's second-largest coal exporter, to reverse course and announce an "overdue coal phaseout date" during the COP31 conference.

"Australia needs to walk the walk and follow Germany's example and commit to a phaseout," said Melanie Pill, founder of The Climate Project, an Australia-based climate policy advisory.

The argument to end fossil fuel production is not only about cutting emissions but reducing dependence on energy systems that rely on volatile oil and gas markets, she explained.

"A fossil phaseout in the face of the enduring and escalating conflict in the Middle East is in the interest of everyone," Pill told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This is especially true for Australia's diesel-reliant Pacific neighbors, who spend up to 25% of GDP on fossil fuel imports — as opposed 6% on health — according to a report by the Institute for Climate Risk and Response at the University of Newly introduced South Wales.

As lead negotiator at the UN climate talks, Australia can "flip the narrative" on a fossil fuel phaseout, using the challenge of energy security as a justification, said Pill.

This opportunity could be lost, however, if Australia fails to address fossil fuel exports that accounted for 80% of its total carbon footprint in 2022 — and near 5% of global emissions.

While the nation is a world leader in rooftop solar, and generates around half of its electricity from renewables, this progress is "being undone by its continued approval of more fossil fuels for export," stated Simon Bradshaw, COP31 lead and climate expert at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

He noted that the Labor government of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has approved the construction, expansion or extension of 38 coal, oil and gas projects since coming to power four years ago on a pro-climate platform.

"You cannot aspire to lead on climate abroad if you're not getting your own house in order," said Thomas Houlie, climate and energy policy analyst at Climate Analytics, a global climate policy institute.

In 2025, when Australia approved the extension of a major gas export project in the country's west until 2070, Albanese justified the move in the name of a balance between "security of energy supply" and "support [for] the transition which reduces our emissions.".

The country has publicly backed a global transition away from the fossil fuels driving the global temperature rise linked to extreme heat and drought. Both through the Global Stocktake agreed at the 2023 UN climate summit, and via the inaugural "transitioning away" summit in Colombia this April, at which Australia and 56 countries pledged to develop a fossil fuel exit road map.

But these commitments are not reflected in Australian resources policy, or its domestic rollout of clean power infrastructure.

"While the government has set a renewables target for electricity, it leaves plenty of blind spots in other sectors," mentioned Houlie, adding that emission reductions in industry and transport have been limited and that the push to achieve an 82% renewables target for the electricity grid by 2030 is behind schedule.

In its role as lead negotiator at COP31, Australia has promised to ensure that any final conference text serves to "elevate the views and the experiences" of small Pacific nations in its region, from Vanuatu to Tuvalu.

These island countries that generate low emissions yet suffer extreme climate impacts from worsening cyclones or rising seas are "sick of Australia's double talk on climate," said Shiva Gounden, head of Pacific at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

Australia must commit to "substantial upcoming funding contributions" to help Pacific neighbors adapt to the climate emergency and achieve energy independence, remarked his colleague Bradshaw. He reiterated the need to concurrently create a "national road map" away from coal and gas production and export.

A Climate Analytics report co-authored by Houlie outlines a fossil fuel phaseout pathway for Australia that can begin immediately. This includes an end to coal power generation by 2034 and a rapid reduction in oil and gas consumption, with renewables generating almost all the country's electricity by 2040. Fossil fuel export projects would be eliminated, and existing ones shuttered before becoming obsolete.

"This co-presidency is a golden opportunity for Australia to step up and commit to a phaseout," mentioned Houlie.

Thomas Frank admits he has a point to prove after taking reins at Crystal Palace

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • ‘I know what I want and the direction we should go in’.
  • Thomas Frank has admitted he has a point to prove on his return to management as he aims to steer Crystal Palace away from relegation trouble after taking over from Pierre Sage.
  • Sources indicate that the Dane was confirmed as manager on Monday with Palace at the bottom of the table after 10 matches having conceded 24 goals – the most in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dane was sacked by Tottenham in February.

‘I know what I want and the direction we should go in’.

Thomas Frank has admitted he has a point to prove on his return to management as he aims to steer Crystal Palace away from relegation trouble after taking over from Pierre Sage.

Sources indicate that the Dane was confirmed as manager on Monday with Palace at the bottom of the table after 10 matches having conceded 24 goals – the most in the Premier League. They face a crucial trip to Coventry on Saturday and Frank said he had been “surprised about how good it feels” after returning to work for the first time since being sacked by ­Tottenham in February.

In a recent development, the 53-year-old spent most of the intervening period travelling, working as a pundit at the World Cup and taking in trips to Japan, Australia and his native Denmark, where he was visiting friends and family when he received the SOS call from Palace last week. Frank previously spent seven years in charge of Brentford but left Spurs after just eight months with a win ratio of 34.2% – the worst of any permanent manager in the club’s history. He believes he has learned from that experience.

Sources indicate that “I think you’ve all got an ego,” he stated. “Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it’s not the critics. It’s more what I can bring myself, what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better. I think that’s the big thing.

Sources indicate that “In this world there’s a lot of clever people out there. But they only know a 10th of the truth. And that’s a 10th of the truth at Brentford and a 10th of the truth at Tottenham. That’s just the way it is – if you can’t handle that as a coach or a player or whatever, then you shouldn’t be in this business. I’m just very happy to be back in the game, very happy to be in a fantastic club, at Palace, where you walk in the door and you just feel the energy. You feel the people. It just feels good.”.

Frank stated he is planning to pick Roy Hodgson’s brains in the coming days after recalling a conversation they had when the former England and Palace manager was still at Selhurst Park.

“I was thinking, does it ever go away? The worry, do you get more relaxed about everything?” he asked Hodgson. “‘No chance, it’s impossible.’ I thought it would have been a little bit easier with age and experience. But in a way can’t help ourselves. I know what I want and the direction we should go in.”.

According to recent reports, justin Cochrane – one of Thomas Tuchel’s assistants for England – has joined as first-team coach and took his first session with Palace on Monday less than 24 hours after the Nations League victory over Spain in Madrid. He is expected to be joined on Palace’s backroom staff by Bernardo Cueva, with Frank confirming that a deal with Chelsea is “very close” for the Mexican. Both worked with Frank at Brentford, where he spent almost nine years as an assistant and then manager. He is also hoping to add Andreas Georgson from Tottenham, who has been credited for his prowess on set-pieces: an area that Palace have struggled with for some time.

But asked whether he will be judged on the perception that his success at Brentford was based on the model that has allowed his successor, Keith Andrews, to thrive since taking over, Frank was not impressed. “Put it this way, I think it was pretty important in terms of building that model,” he said.

  • Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station. Recently, NASA astronaut and Crew-13 commander Jessica Watkins got to work supporting an ongoing experiment that includes 3D-printing human cells and tissues in space.

Aboard the space station, astronauts have a multitude of responsibilities ranging from station maintenance and repairs on spacewalks to daily exercise and a wide variety of scientific research.

Watkins recently shared a snapshot captured by her crewmate Anil Menon that showcases her experience working on an experiment called InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing that takes place inside the station's Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research space and one of Watkins favorite places to work on the space station, she shared on social media.

In the image she is gloved-up with both her hands and arms covered in the sealed glovebox while she mixes samples of living cells with a bioink, a mixture she then inserts into a specialized cartridge, NASA shared.

Industry observers note that this experiment that Watkins is working on "leverages the microgravity environment of ISS to 3D print cells and manufacture human liver, kidney, and cartilage tissue. Just one of many examples of how we’re using this amazing orbital national laboratory to reshape our understanding of biology, medicine, and engineering, and improve life on Earth!" Watkins shared online.

Recent findings suggest that this experiment is designed to explore 3D printing human cartilage tissue in microgravity. The experiment aims to one day support future human patients both in space and on Earth.

Sources indicate that when you think of the research that happens in space, 3D-printing human cells might not be the first thing to come to mind. But because of the unique microgravity environment onboard the ISS, it is the perfect home for even the strangest of biological experiments.

Industry observers note that on the space station, there is still gravity but objects (and people) remain in a sort of constant freefall, leading to total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This weightlessness allows researchers to test, experiment and explore beyond the gravitational confines of Earth.

With a M.S. in Biology, Chelsea has written and worked for institutions including NASA JPL, the American Museum of Natural History, Scientific American, Discover Magazine Blog, Astronomy Magazine, and Live Science. When not writing, editing or filming something space-y, Gohd is writing music and performing as Foxanne, even launching a song to space in 2021 with Inspiration4. Are Liverpool prepared for Grand Theft Auto to ruin their weekend preparation?

Ah s***, here we go again: GTA VI dropped this week to rapturous acclaim from critics and public alike, with the long-awaited video game responsible for plenty of us turning up to work a little bleary-eyed after an all-nighter in Vice City.

And given that Premier League footballers are often avid gamers – they have a lot of time on their hands – FPL players are going to have to take into account those last-minute “groin strains” that see big-hitters pull out of this weekend's action….

Industry observers note that in September 2013, Liverpool defender Daniel Agger suffered a freak abdominal injury when he overstretched to prevent a dumbbell from falling on his foot in training. Or did he?

No, he probably did: but while the story certainly made sense – and Agger even aggravated the injury after playing through the pain barrier – the fact that Grand Theft Auto V was released that week certainly led some to wonder whether the Dane had in fact pulled a sickie.

Agger was far from the only suspicious absentee that week in the league either, with high-profile names missing up and down the country.

Robin van Persie and David Silva both missed the Manchester derby, completely unexpectedly, with the stars ruled out late with sudden muscle injuries: Manchester United boss David Moyes even revealed that he'd given RVP the chance to play right up until that Sunday morning.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Theo Walcott was even named in Arsenal's starting line-up for Stoke City that weekend, but pulled out with a mysterious “abdominal concern”, paving the way for Serge Gnabry to step in, while Gareth Bale was expected to make his Real Madrid debut that weekend, only for a “thigh tweak” in the warm-up to rule him out.

Silva and Walcott both missed the following fixtures – suggesting they really did have an alibi, with the latter requiring surgery – though Van Persie and Bale both recovered to make the bench the following week (convenient).

Regardless, there will be plenty of speculation this time around when line-ups are revealed as to who's really injured and who's spent all week on the console and not in a fit state for high-level football.

Premier League action resumes this weekend with all 20 teams in action.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that england have been handed a ­suspended ­one-match ban on away ticket sales by Uefa in relation to “­racist and/or ­discriminatory” behaviour by fans at Sunday’s 3-2 Nations League victory over Spain.
  • It has been revealed that uefa has also fined the Football Association €15,000 (£12,500), with the behaviour in question believed to be the chant of “Fuck the pope and the IRA” at the ­Metropolitano ­Stadium in Madrid.
  • The FA said in a statement: “We will not ­tolerate this unacceptable and deeply ­offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all ­England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ban by Uefa is suspended for two years.

Uefa also fines FA £12,500 for offensive chants.

Industry observers note that england have been handed a ­suspended ­one-match ban on away ticket sales by Uefa in relation to “­racist and/or ­discriminatory” behaviour by fans at Sunday’s 3-2 Nations League victory over Spain. The punishment is suspended for two years.

It has been revealed that uefa has also fined the Football Association €15,000 (£12,500), with the behaviour in question believed to be the chant of “Fuck the pope and the IRA” at the ­Metropolitano ­Stadium in Madrid. A further charge in the next two years could trigger a ban on away fans for a competitive game.

The FA said in a statement: “We will not ­tolerate this unacceptable and deeply ­offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all ­England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.”.

Uefa’s control, ­ethics and ­disciplinary body unveiled that it had decided “to fine the English ­Football ­Association €15,000 and to order against the ­English Football Association a full ­restriction on selling tickets to its ­supporters for one representative team competition away match, for the ­racist and/or discriminatory ­behaviour of its supporters.

“Mentioned full restriction on selling tickets to supporters for one away match is suspended for a ­probationary period of two years, starting from the date of the present decision.”.

The relevant article of Uefa’s disciplinary regulations reads: “If one or more of a member association or club’s supporters engage in the behaviour described in paragraph 1 [insulting the human dignity of a person or group of persons on whatever grounds, including skin colour, race, religion, ethnic origin, gender or ­sexual orientation], the ­member association or club ­responsible incurs a minimum of a fine and either a ­partial stadium closure or a ­restriction on selling tickets to its supporters for away matches.”.

In a recent development, in the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

The match had been preceded by Thomas Tuchel reminding his players of the anti-­racism protocols, given the last match between the sides in Madrid, in 2004, had notoriously been marred by abuse aimed at England’s black players.

Last month Spain were fined £15,000 and ordered to play their next friendly with a partial stadium closure after discriminatory chants about Muslims during March’s match against Egypt in Barcelona.

According to recent reports, sunday’s chant is a staple for some England fans but sung relatively rarely in stadiums. Several more frequently heard chants target only the IRA, including inserting “No surrender” into the national anthem.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will spend the coming weeks in a medical boot after tearing his Achilles tendon in a pickup soccer match against the City Hall press corps on Thursday night.

Arriving at a Friday news conference on crutches, the 35-year-old leader explained how the injury occurred minutes into Thursday’s game when he was questioned by a reporter.

As for what caused the injury, the millennial leader of America's biggest city pointed to a neglected pre-game warmup, admitting: "I did not stretch.".

Nevertheless, the avid soccer fan was pleased to share that he scored a goal "soon after getting on the pitch" before noting that he "forgot that I was 35.".

He was also quick to point out that his team ultimately beat the journalists' squad.

The mayor, known for keeping a busy schedule, stated he will wear the medical boot for six to eight weeks and expects to be back on the pitch in about nine months.

Mamdani has made no secret of the fact that he is a huge Arsenal fan, the current English Premier League champions.

Mamdani has displayed his affection for the Gunners, who pipped City for the title last season to break a 22-year drought, in recent months, including an appearance at Eid al-Adha prayers in the Bronx while wearing a club-themed kurta.

Mamdani recalled supporting Arsenal from the age of nine thanks to his uncle and idolised players such as Tony Adams and, particularly, Nwankwo Kanu, given the Nigerian “had been born in Africa but now lived somewhere else, just like me.”.

Mamdani told the New York Times about how Arsenal had become an escape for him and recalled the intense battles with City in recent seasons: “Over these past two years, no matter how chaotic life became, Arsenal remained the constant.

Recent findings suggest that “And throughout every moment, when a Manchester City resurgence felt inevitable, when the socialist project felt fragile, when both football and politics appeared determined to reward only wealth and cynicism, I have returned to the words of a man with no enemies: Bukayo Saka. ‘It’s a process.’ And we should trust it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft.
  • The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov.
  • NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft.

The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov. 17), the day before Voyager 1 gets one light-day from Earth. And that's a big milestone: One light-day is the distance light travels in a day — about 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers).

NASA is encouraging "Shine Bright" participants to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft's three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code, according to a statement from the space agency.

Sources indicate that to celebrate the spacecraft, participants can use a flashlight, phone, bike light or other portable light source to send the signal skyward. And don't fret if you're unfamiliar with Morse code: NASA has created an automated flasher that can be opened in a smartphone or tablet browser to display the VGR sequence.

Recent findings suggest that the spacecraft’s call sign pattern consists of three quick flashes followed by one long flash for the letter V, two long flashes and one quick flash for G, and one quick flash, one long flash and another quick flash for R. Participants are encouraged to repeat the sequence for about a minute, NASA officials noted.

Sources indicate that NASA also invites people to photograph or record their light signals and share them on social media, tagging the agency's official account, @NASA. The goal is to create a worldwide display of light marking a milestone nearly five decades in the making.

Industry observers note that the celebration is intended as a symbolic tribute rather than an actual attempt to communicate with Voyager 1. At a distance of one light-day from Earth, the spacecraft is so far away that even radio signals traveling at the speed of light take approximately 24 hours to reach it. A flashlight or phone signal from Earth, of course, cannot reach the probe; NASA communicates with it using its Deep Space Network of radio dishes.

Debuted on Sept. 5, 1977, Voyager 1 has spent nearly 50 years traveling through space and is now the most distant human-made object from Earth. When it reaches the one-light-day milestone, it will have traveled a distance that light itself takes 24 hours to cross. Its twin, Voyager 2, is expected to reach the same milestone in November 2035. (The two spacecraft took different routes through the solar system.).

Sources indicate that the public celebration will be followed by another opportunity to learn more about the historic mission. On Thursday (Nov. 19) at 12 p.m. EST (1700 GMT), NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California will host a moderated discussion with Voyager mission team members and NASA leadership.

Sources indicate that the discussion will cover the current status of both Voyager spacecraft, the unique scientific observations they continue to collect in interstellar space and the engineering challenges involved in keeping the nearly 50-year-old probes operational. A question-and-answer session with members of the media and audience will follow. NASA will also offer a preview of an upcoming Voyager documentary planned for release in 2027, coinciding with the mission's 50th anniversary.

For a mission that has carried humanity's message into interstellar space for nearly half a century, the "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day” offers a chance for people back on Earth to mark just how far these pioneering spacecraft have traveled. More details about NASA's automated VGR flasher and step-by-step Morse code instructions are available online.

Samantha Mathewson joined Space.com as an intern in the summer of 2016. She received a B.A. in Journalism and Environmental Science at the University of New Haven, in Connecticut. Previously, her work has been published in Nature World News. When not writing or reading about science, Samantha enjoys traveling to new places and taking photos! You can follow her on Twitter @Sam_Ashley13.

  • I sat with her and I told her: 'Listen, I don't think I can play any more'," says Dejan Kulusevski in a moving interview about his injury nightmare.
  • It is 18 months since Tottenham and Sweden winger Kulusevski, 26, last started a competitive match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham have played 50 Premier League games since Dejan Kulusevski's last top-flight start in May 2025.

"I told my mother. I sat with her and I told her: 'Listen, I don't think I can play any more'," says Dejan Kulusevski in a moving interview about his injury nightmare.

It is 18 months since Tottenham and Sweden winger Kulusevski, 26, last started a competitive match.

Spurs have won the Europa League, sacked both Ange Postecoglou and Thomas Frank, "mutually agreed" to part ways with Igor Tudor and appointed Roberto de Zerbi since the former Juventus player last started a first-team game for his club.

A serious knee injury two weeks from the end of the 2024-25 season forced him to miss the whole of the following campaign, as well as the 2026 World Cup.

"You feel like the whole world has forgotten about you," adds Kulusevski in an interview with Tottenham's in-house media, external about the emotional toll of being out for so long.

Thankfully, the player nicknamed 'Deki' has made a full recovery and is closing in on his first Tottenham start since 11 May 2025.

He is not the only footballer to question their career after having their world turned upside down by injury.

In the women's game, Everton club captain Megan Finnigan recently returned from a cruciate ligament injury after 602 days out., external.

"The amount of times the thought of retirement entered my head during rehab was a lot," Finnigan, 28, tells BBC Sport.

Countless hours in the gym away from team-mates, boredom, setbacks and frustration - what is it like for a player at the peak of their game to miss a season because of injury?

'I am a different man now' - Kulusevski on return after 526 days.

Kulusevski out for a 'few months' - Postecoglou.

Before Crystal Palace visited Tottenham a fortnight from the end of the 2024-25 campaign, Kulusevski had much to look forward to.

Off the pitch, he was making looks to marry his partner Eldina Ahmic, a former midfielder with Swedish club Brommapojkarna and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

On the pitch, there was a Europa League final against Manchester United coming up.

Everything changed in that match against Palace.

In the early stages, Kulusevski stayed down after a challenge with Marc Guehi. He was able to climb to his feet and walk unaided off the pitch and straight down the tunnel.

But in that moment, his problems were only just starting.

Start of a nightmare for Dejan Kulusevski who goes down injured in May 2025 - and does not play again until October 2026.

"It was pain, but it didn't hurt that much," Kulusevski says, recalling the patella and cartilage injury in his right knee.

"I could feel that the knee was moving a little bit too much.".

The initial diagnosis from Tottenham was that the Â£25m signing from Juventus, who arrived in the summer of 2023, would be out for "at least a few months".

Due to complications, those months turned into a year and Kulusevski's dream career threatened to turn into a nightmare.

He travelled to Bilbao on crutches to watch his team-mates beat United in the Europa League final.

"That was one of the hardest days of my life," he states. "It was so beautiful to see all the people happy, but for me I was going there with crutches, I couldn't work.

"I couldn't even go and get my medal because it was too slippy to go on that thing [platform].

"Seeing the team celebrating on the bus [outside Tottenham Hotspur Stadium] was probably one of the most difficult parts of this journey because you feel so alone.

"You feel like the whole world has forgot about you and what you put in.".

As months went by, Kulusevski underwent multiple operations and was even offered a knee transplant as a treatment option, which he rejected.

"You get stressed because nothing works," he says.

Then came another crushing blow delivered in a phone call with Sweden boss Graham Potter. Stockholm-born Kulusevski, who had played for his country since the age of 19, would not be going to the 2026 World Cup.

He had hoped to recover in time to be selected.

"I just stared at the wall for three hours because I really believed I would do it," he states.

It is not just the players who suffer when they are out for so long; the people around them feel the emotional toll as well.

"Seeing him miss the Europa League final and the World Cup, every Premier League game last season, seeing him skipping around on his crutches, those parts were really difficult," Eldina, Kulusevski's wife, claims.

'Fantastic moment, fantastic human' - De Zerbi on Kulusevski's long-awaited return.

As recently as this past summer, Kulusevski wondered whether he would play again.

"It had been one year and two months and I could still not walk up the stairs like a normal guy.

"I wasn't going to give up, but I also had to think if this didn't work out, what am I going to do, because I am 26 and I have to have some sort of plan.".

Enormous comfort came from Leonie, Kulusevski's two-year-old daughter, during his bleakest days.

"I remarked if I cannot play football any more, I will still have fun with her.".

Then, after multiple setbacks, came a crucial breakthrough.

His knee had healed sufficiently for specialists to give him permission to train again.

On 19 October, Kulusevski was given a hero's reception by Spurs fans when he made his first appearance in 526 days.

It came in Tottenham's 3-1 win over Coventry City as an 87th-minute substitute.

Waiting for him after the final whistle were Eldina and Leonie, his daughter wearing a Spurs shirt with the number 526 on the back, along with the words 'My Hero'.

He made his Sweden return this month, coming off the bench in a win against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

"Every day is just beautiful now," says Kulusevski, who has made four substitute appearances totalling 42 minutes for his club this season.

"I don't take it for granted any more.".

Research suggests female footballers are two to six times more likely to suffer anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries than their male counterparts.

Everton captain Finnigan remembers how she "completely lost my sparkle" as she endured the long road to recovery.

"It's not comfortable to think back how I was," Finnigan tells BBC Radio Merseyside's Giulia Bould.

Industry observers note that "Anyone that knows me knows I'm very bubbly, quite loud, I like to be at the centre of things. I completely lost myself in rehab, completely lost my sparkle as my mum notes.

Sources indicate that "How I was in this building is not nice to think back on. I was always thinking what other people were thinking about me. I was not pleasant to be around as I was struggling so much.

Sources indicate that "I was also thinking 'no-one wants to be around me'. I was just miserable. Everyone in this building has seen me cry over the past 18 months.".

Listen: Megan Finnigan 'Really special feeling to be back'.

Megan Finnigan, Everton's number 20, returned to competitive action this season after 602 days out following an ACL injury.

Finnigan - Everton's longest-serving women's player having joined the Blues at the age of nine - suffered her injury in an FA Cup tie against Tottenham in January 2025. She did not return to competitive action until September of this year.

"I was in quite a difficult place mentally," she adds.

One thing that helped her through her lowest moments was writing down her feelings.

"It was an absolute whirlwind of a rehab, a rollercoaster," she adds.

In a recent development, "Anyone who went through it with me will tell you that. I am really glad I kept a diary as proof I did it and survived it.".

Former Arsenal and England midfielder Fara Williams points to how some players who suffer serious injuries in the Women's Super League face specific worries.

"While they are going through rehab, there are financial worries, bills to pay; they are on short contracts so you don't have that stability," states Williams.

In a recent development, "While you are managing the injury, mentally you are stressing, wondering where the next contract is coming from. When you are stressed, I imagine that doesn't help with the healing of the injury.".

Micah Richards suffered multiple long-term knee and hamstring injuries before he retired in 2019 while at Aston Villa.

A few months later the former Manchester City and England defender opened up to BBC Sport about injuries and the "dark side of football".

"I was in a lonely place for a long time, and I did not know how to get out of it," he noted at the time.

"Deep down, I probably knew it was already over, but for most of the two and a half years between my 295th and final game as a professional, against Wolves in October 2016, and the day I unveiled my retirement in July 2019, I was living in denial.

"I could run and I could jump - but I couldn't twist on my right knee, and it would not get any better. Whatever I tried, it did not make any difference.

"There were times while I was injured at Villa when I felt like I was a ghost.

Industry observers note that "They told me to come in three times a week, then two. Then one.

"I would go into the gym and tell myself 'I am all right, I am all right, I am all right' but actually I had no idea how to deal with what was happening to me, and my body.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Get-in price peaked at $755 before dropping to $362.

Previous NWSL finals never topped $100 on matchday.

Analyst cites Spirit home game and thin resale supply.

The get-in price for tickets to Saturday’s NWSL Championship match plunged more than 50% this week but was still set to finish at more than three times the previous record for an NWSL final.

After the Washington Spirit booked their spot in the final against the Kansas City Current with a semi-final victory last Saturday, the get-in price for the championship match spiked as high as $755 that same night, according to TicketData.com. However, that price had dropped as low as $308 on Friday morning before climbing back to $362 by midday.

Industry observers note that while representing a 52.1% drop from Saturday’s high, the get-in price for previous NWSL championship matches has never settled higher than $100, according to TicketData.com. Last year’s championship match between the Spirit and Gotham FC in San Jose settled at a get-in price of $64.

Industry observers note that the Spirit will be playing in their home stadium at Audi Field, contributing to the record ticket-price pace. Unlike most playoff matches, the NWSL Championship is awarded to a host city well in advance, making the Spirit’s appearance in the final a particularly fortunate coincidence for the league. Kansas City earned their spot with a dramatic 2-1 win over Gotham FC on Sunday afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that US ticketing analyst Keith Smith described the extraordinary prices as a “perfect storm”, pointing to the Spirit’s home-field advantage and unusually limited ticket availability on the resale market. Because NWSL matches have not traditionally attracted significant interest from ticket resellers, he stated on social media, there has been little inventory available on secondary-market platforms throughout the week.

Industry observers note that for comparison, the get-in price for last year’s MLS Cup, won by Inter Miami in South Florida, settled at $271 after peaking at $806. Smith noted that tickets for that match, featuring Lionel Messi, were available in the mid-$200s on match day – considerably less than the cheapest seats for Saturday’s NWSL final.

Industry observers note that smith also pointed to the record prices for this year’s WNBA finals as further evidence of the growing commercial appeal of women’s sports. The two championship events, taking place just weeks apart, have underscored a surge in demand that would have been difficult to imagine in previous years, when NWSL final did not always sell out.

NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said this week that high ticket prices for the championship represent a “good problem to have”.

  • In a recent development, in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, electrification isn't just a buzzword, it's a lever that could slash energy bills while reducing the world's dependency on coal, oil and gas. Which also means significantly slashing the heat-trapping CO2 emissions that are linked to flooding and extreme heat around the world.

Recent findings suggest that if fuel-importing countries "speed up the electrification of their economies considerably" they could knock more than $400 billion (€357 billion) off their energy import bills by 2035 compared with 2025 levels. That is according to a recent analysis by the International Energy Agency, which also found that such an acceleration could mean the world needs 18 million fewer barrels of oil per day.

In a recent development, in a nutshell, electrification means replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels such as oil and gas with electric alternatives. That means switching from diesel cars to electric vehicles (EVs), turning off gas heating and using electricity to power heat pumps.

But the way the electricity running these things is generated is also key. In theory, an EV using power created in a coal-heavy electricity grid could be worse for the climate than a car running on gas.

Electricity derived from renewable energy sources such as solar, wind or hydropower on the other hand produces clean power.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The booming EV market is the fastest-growing electrification sector. Globally, one in four cars sold in 2025 was electric and since 2020, international sales have increased by almost 600%.

Nonetheless, electricity only covers about 20% of final energy use in the wider global economy, including that used in businesses, factories and people's homes.

It would need to supply more than half of all power by 2050 if we are to avoid runaway heating and the more intense and extreme weather events connected to a hotter climate.

Some industries and activities are harder to electrify than others. While it's relatively easy to switch to EVs and decarbonize buildings, some industries such as petrochemicals and steel use fossil fuels as raw materials to make products like plastics, fertilizer, detergent or steel.

In addition, while heat pumps work well for low-temperature needs, they can't replace the temperatures needed in steelmaking or cement production.

The World Resources Institute, an independent research organization, recommends hydrogen, synthetic fuels or other low-carbon alternatives as more viable options than electrification in cases such as ocean shipping and aviation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In addition to cutting down on greenhouse gas emissions resulting in cleaner air and limiting global heating, electrification is also more efficient and cheaper in the long run.

In a recent development, A combustion engine in a car wastes as much as 80% of its fuel energy, mostly to turn it into heat. Only about 20% is converted to actually move the car. Electric motors, on the other hand, convert about 80% of electrical energy into motion.

Recent findings suggest that as the World Resources Institute points out, running all appliances on electricity will increase electricity consumption. Yet total energy costs are likely to be lower, even if electricity becomes more expensive.

As electricity needs grow due to the rapid expansion of AI, data centers and the overall shift to a more electrified world, outpaced grids struggle to keep up. This is increasingly holding back the energy transition, delaying the rollout of additional renewable generation, storage capacity and electrified demand.

According to the International Energy Agency, annual grid investment has to increase by about 50% by 2030 from today's $400 billion.

There's also a major mismatch between how long it takes to set up fresh grid infrastructure (five to 15 years), compared to renewable energy projects (one to five years), and EV charging infrastructure (one to two years).

Experts say we need smarter grids that support a two-way flow of electricity while remaining secure, stable and able to keep up with higher demand as electrification intensifies.

Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal.

Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season.

An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that season and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations.

Eckert accepted responsibility as Southampton opted to stand by their manager despite the controversy, and he was later given a six-week suspended ban - keeping him on the touchline barring any further offences.

And despite the hindrance of a points deduction, Southampton have started the season in fine form under Eckert, with the club five points off top spot.

The German has now been rewarded with a contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2029.

Eckert mentioned: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now.

"There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come.".

Saints are unbeaten in their last 17 home matches, with Eckert only experiencing one defeat at St Mary’s during his tenure.

"I think it's a great commitment from both sides; from the club to Tonda, and from Tonda to the club. I'm very happy that we have achieved this agreement before the end of the international window, allowing us to go into the busy schedule that is ahead of us with clarity,” sporting director Johannes Spors remarked.

"Tonda is very talented and very precise with a great analytical brain, but also has the personality and authority that you need, even at a young age. It is very clear that this is the right place for him, and I'm very happy that he feels that too.".

Man accused of abusing former Bournemouth winger.

Alleged incident happened at Anfield game in 2025.

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the Manchester City forward withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool magistrates court on Friday in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting abuse during the Premier League match between Liverpool and Semenyo’s former club Bournemouth at Anfield on 15 August last year.

According to recent reports, but Simon Jones, prosecuting, stated: “Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him. In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.”.

District judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

Semenyo, who left Bournemouth for Manchester City in January, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mogan was taken to hospital after a seizure.

It has been revealed that the court had heard Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted racial abuse at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game. He was alleged to have remarked: “Hurry up and take the throw-in, you black bastard.”.

Opening the case last month, Mr Jones stated: “That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him. Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn’t believe what the male had said.”.

Sources indicate that mogan then shouted: “I’m talking to you, you cunt,” the court heard. Witnesses also stated they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the referee and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time. Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to “hurry up”.

Mogan declined to comment as he left court.

#59415. On this day in space! Nov. 17, 1967: NASA's Surveyor 6 moon probe makes 1st-ever successful launch and hop from the lunar surface

On this day in space! Nov. 17, 1967: NASA's Surveyor 6 moon probe makes 1st-ever successful launch and hop from the lunar surface

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (704 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that surveyor 6 was one of several robotic lunar missions NASA sent to scout the moon before sending humans there.
  • It has been revealed that first Surveyor 6 launched from the surface and hopped to another position about 8 feet (2 meters) away.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on Nov. 17, 1967, NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft made the first liftoff from the lunar surface.

Sources indicate that surveyor 6 was one of several robotic lunar missions NASA sent to scout the moon before sending humans there. It took television pictures of the surface and learned about the composition of lunar soil. Then came the massive liftoff.

It has been revealed that first Surveyor 6 launched from the surface and hopped to another position about 8 feet (2 meters) away. Next, Surveyor 6 took pictures of its original landing site. Flight controllers on Earth could see the landing pad prints of Surveyor 6. They also saw an imprint from the rocket exhaust when Surveyor 6 lifted off.

Surveyor 6 highlighted that spacecraft could land on the moon, and lift off again. Less than two years later, humans did the same thing during Apollo 11.

Industry observers note that NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft released to the moon on Nov. 7, 1967 and made its first landing on the lunar surface on Nov. 10 of that year. It's primary mission was to make a soft landing on the moon in the Sinus Medii of the moon.

Sources indicate that the probe took nearly 30,000 photos of the moon during its 16 days on the lunar surface, with the lander shutting down due to the onset of lunar night on Nov. 26. Surveyor 6 was the sixth and penultimate moon mission of NASA's Surveyor lunar program, so a lot of what it did (launching and landing on the moon) had been done before.

But a lunar liftoff? That was something upcoming.

"On November 17, as an engineering test to see if its rockets could be restarted on the Moon, Surveyor’s engines fired for 2.5 seconds, lifting the spacecraft 12 feet high and moving it 8 feet west of its original landing site, in the first powered liftoff from another celestial body," NASA wrote in a mission overview.

Industry observers note that the engineering test proved that a spacecraft could land on the moon, and then lift off and take flight once more. That capability was a core requirement for NASA's Apollo astronaut moon landings that followed, since astronauts needed a way to return home after visiting the moon.

But there was critical science Surveyor 6 was able to do with the lunar hop.

"This maneuver provided excellent views of the surface disturbances produced by the initial landing and the effects of firing rocket engines close to the lunar surface," scientists with the Lunar and Planetary Institute wrote in a summary. "Photography obtained after the hop contributed to the soil mechanics investigation.".

Surveyor 6 also had a bar magnet on its footpad that allowed scientists to test how magnetic the lunar regolith was at the landing site.

Sources indicate that want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She at the moment lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

#59414. Breaking: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (852 w)
📖 Baca

Breaking: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.
  • According to recent reports, "Faith does not justify exclusion.
  • "In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related concerns and the athletic performance of individual players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Felix Nmecha's renewed use of the "Crowns down celebration" — where a crown is pretended to be removed from someone's head and placed at Jesus' feet — has sparked a reaction from Borussia Dortmund's official supporters' group.

According to recent reports, "Faith does not justify exclusion. Faith does not justify division. Borussia Dortmund is a club for everyone," read a statement after the Bundesliga club beat Elversberg, a game in which Nmecha scored twice. Nmecha's first documented "Crowns down celebration" was at the 2026 World Cup, for which "The King's Return" campaign was released.

"In the past, the the Borussia Dortmund supporters club has deliberately refrained from commenting on sports-related concerns and the athletic performance of individual players. We remain committed to this approach," the statement continued.

"However, when it comes to our club's values, discrimination, and the question of what view of humanity is fostered within and around Borussia Dortmund, we cannot and will not remain silent.".

The fan club states their concern is not with Nmecha being a devout Christian, but rather his public support for "The King's Return" campaign, which the supporters club noted "gives us cause to reassess the situation.".

Sources indicate that this campaign, according to research by German public broadcaster ARD in the summer of 2026, was designed by the "Ballers in God" (SIGNIFICANT) network. BIG was founded in 2015 by footballer John Bostock, a devout Christian who wanted to create a community where professional footballers could strengthen each other in their faith, pray together, and read the Bible. In over a decade since, the BIG community has grown to nearly 800,000 followers on Instagram.

Nmecha issued a response on social media not long afterwards, writing:.

"I've been told that my most recent goal celebration has led to some misunderstandings," Nmecha wrote.

"My message was never intended to spread intolerance, discrimination, or hatred in any form. As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for every person—regardless of where someone comes from, what they believe in, or what worldview they hold.".

Reports suggest that both the board at Dortmund and Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp will speak to Nmecha on the matter in the coming days.

In a recent development, the fan club say their criticism is "directed at religious networks that, under the guise of faith, promote a worldview in which people are devalued or marginalized because of their sexual orientation, gender identity, lifestyle, or personal choices... When religious beliefs are used to deny people their dignity or equality, that is where our tolerance for intolerance ends.".

Here, they are referring to the recent ARD investigation. That work revealed the homepage for "The King's Return" campaign featured a link to a live counseling chat run by US-based evangelical nonprofit Groundwire. During the investigations, counselors told reporters that abortion is "Satan's initiative" and that homosexuality is a sin.

It has been revealed that borussia Dortmund's statement of core values commits the club to diversity, human rights, and inclusion regardless of gender, sexual orientation, faith, or background. The club's largest and most influential fan group also promotes progressive, anti-fascist, and inclusive values. It is also part of a wider fan landscape in Germany where club members are more involved in club decisions than in many other countries. This was evidenced when the club signed a deal with arms manufacturer Rheinmetall two years ago and in the case of Nmecha as well. When the midfielder signed for Dortmund in 2023, many of the club's fans protested because the player had previously shared or liked several transphobic and homophobic posts on his Instagram account. In response, Nmecha deleted some posts and instead issued a statement emphasizing "I do not discriminate against anyone.".

Article 4 of German Basic Law guarantees that each individual is allowed to decide how strongly, why and which god to believe in. In football, players cannot display political, religious, or personal slogans, statements, or images on their jerseys, undershirts, or gear. However, physical gestures are allowed so long as they don't delay the game or antagonize the crowd.

The use of physical religious gestures has history in sports, as professor Paul Putz described in his book "The Spirit of the Game: American Christianity and Substantial-Time Sports". Putz describes how the the pioneers of the Christian athlete movement realized they: "could influence others to Christian ideals more effectively on the field than in the pulpit.".

It has been revealed that and yet, such gestures can also be at odds with the atmosphere of modern sports arenas, particularly football. In their book "Sports and Christianity: Historical and Contemporary Perspectives", Nick J. Watson and Andrew Parker explain how modern sport has become a substitute for traditional faith.

"Sport seduces the teeming 'global village'; it is the latest opiate of the masses; it is one of the great modern experiences … Sport, for many, has replaced religion as a source of emotional catharsis and spiritual passion," they wrote.

With the 26-year-old Nmecha a key player for both club and country, the conversation around faith and football looks set to continue for some time yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Editor’s Note:  This story was originally published in April 2023.

Slumped on his club, head buried in his arm, Rory McIlroy looked on the verge of tears.

The then-21-year-old had just watched his ball sink into the waters of Rae’s Creek at Augusta National and with it, his dream of winning The Masters, a dream that had looked so tantalizingly close mere hours earlier.

As a four-time major winner and one of the most decorated names in the sport’s history, few players would turn down the chance to swap places with McIlroy heading into Augusta this week.

Yet on Sunday afternoon of April 10, 2011, not a golfer in the world would have wished to be in the Northern Irishman’s shoes.

A fresh-faced, mop-headed McIlroy had touched down in Georgia for the first major of the season with a reputation as the leading light of the next generation of stars.

An excellent 2010 had marked his best season since turning pro three years earlier, highlighted by a first PGA Tour win at the Quail Hollow Championship and a crucial contribution to Team Europe’s triumph at the Ryder Cup.

Yet despite a pair of impressive top-three finishes at the Open and PGA Championship respectively, a disappointing missed cut at The Masters – his first at a major – served as ominous foreshadowing.

McIlroy shot 74 and 77 to fall four strokes short of the cut line at seven-over par, a performance that concerned him enough to take a brief sabbatical from competition.

But one year on in 2011, any lingering Masters demons looked to have been exorcised as McIlroy flew round the Augusta fairways.

Having opened with a bogey-free seven-under 65 – the first time he had ever shot in the 60s at the major – McIlroy pulled ahead from Spanish first round co-leader Alvaro Quirós with a second round 69.

It sent him into the weekend holding a two-shot cushion over Australia’s Jason Day, with Tiger Woods a further stroke behind and back in the hunt for a 15th major after a surging second round 66.

According to recent reports, and yet the 21-year-old leader looked perfectly at ease with having a target on his back. Even after a tentative start to the third round, McIlroy rallied with three birdies across the closing six holes to stretch his lead to four strokes heading into Sunday.

Industry observers note that the youngster was out on his own ahead of a bunched chasing pack comprising Day, Ángel Cabrera, K.J. Choi and Charl Schwartzel. After 54 holes, McIlroy had shot just three bogeys.

“It’s a great position to be in … I’m finally feeling comfortable on this golf course,” McIlroy told reporters.

In a recent development, “I’m not getting ahead of myself, I know how leads can dwindle away very swiftly. I have to go out there, not take anything for granted and go out and play as hard as I’ve played the last three days. If I can do that, hopefully things will go my way.

“We’ll see what happens tomorrow because four shots on this golf course isn’t that much.”.

The truth can hurt, and McIlroy was about to prove his assessment of Augusta to be true in the most excruciating way imaginable.

His fourth bogey of the week arrived immediately. Having admitted to expecting some nerves at the first tee, McIlroy sparked a booming opening drive down the fairway, only to miss his putt from five feet.

Industry observers note that three consecutive pars steadied the ship, but Schwartzel had the wind in his sails. A blistering birdie, par, eagle start had seen him draw level at the summit after his third hole.

A subsequent bogey from the South African slowed his charge, as McIlroy clung onto a one-shot lead at the turn from Schwartzel, Cabrera, Choi, and a rampaging Woods, who shot five birdies and an eagle across the front nine to send Augusta into a frenzy.

Despite his dwindling advantage and the raucous Tiger-mania din ahead of him, McIlroy had responded well to another bogey at the 5th hole, draining a brilliant 20-foot putt at the 7th to restore his lead.

The fist pump that followed marked the high-water point of McIlroy’s round, as a sliding start accelerated into full-blown free-fall at the par-four 10th hole.

His tee shot went careening into a tree, ricocheting to settle between the white cabins that separate the main course from the adjacent par-three course. It offered viewers a glimpse at a part of Augusta rarely seen on broadcast, followed by pictures of McIlroy anxiously peering out from behind a tree to track his follow-up shot.

Though his initial escape was successful, yet another collision with a tree and a two-putt on the green saw a stunned McIlroy eventually tap in for a triple bogey. Having led the field one hole and seven shots earlier, he arrived at the 11th tee in seventh.

By the time his tee drive at the 13th plopped into the creek, all thoughts of who might be the recipient of the green jacket had long-since switched away from the anguished youngster. It had taken him seven putts to navigate the previous two greens, as a bogey and a double bogey dropped him to five-under – the score he had held after just 11 holes of the tournament.

It has been revealed that mercifully, the last five holes passed without major incident. A missed putt for birdie from five feet at the final hole summed up McIlroy’s day, though he was given a rousing reception as he left the green.

Mere minutes earlier, the same crowd had erupted as Schwartzel sunk his fourth consecutive birdie to seal his first major title. After starting the day four shots adrift of McIlroy, the South African finished 10 shots ahead of him, and two ahead of second-placed Australian duo Jason Day and Adam Scott.

In a recent development, mcIlroy’s eight-over 80 marked the highest score of the round. Having headlined the leaderboard for most of the week, he finished tied-15th.

Tears would flow during a phone call with his parents the following morning, but at his press conference, McIlroy was upbeat.

“I’m very disappointed at the minute, and I’m sure I will be for the next few days, but I’ll get over it,” he remarked.

“I was leading this golf tournament with nine holes to go, and I just unraveled … It’s a Sunday at a major, what it can do.

“This is my first experience at it, and hopefully the next time I’m in this position I’ll be able to handle it a little better. I didn’t handle it particularly well today obviously, but it was a character-building day … I’ll come out stronger for it.”.

Once again, McIlroy would be proven right.

Sources indicate that just eight weeks later in June, McIlroy rampaged to an eight-shot victory at the US Open. Records tumbled in his wake at Congressional, as he shot a tournament record 16-under 268 to become the youngest major winner since Tiger Woods at The Masters in 1997.

The historic victory kickstarted a golden era for McIlroy. After coasting to another eight-shot win at the PGA Championship in 2012, McIlroy became only the third golfer since 1934 to win three majors by the age of 25 with triumph at the 2014 Open Championship.

Before the year was out, he would add his fourth major title with another PGA Championship win.

And much of it was owed to that fateful afternoon at Augusta. In an interview with the BBC in 2015, McIlroy dubbed it “the most key day” of his career.

“If I had not had the whole unravelling, if I had just made a couple of bogeys coming down the stretch and lost by one, I would not have learned as much.

“Luckily, it did not take me long to get into a position like that again when I was leading a major and I was able to get over the line quite comfortably. It was a huge learning curve for me and I needed it, and thankfully I have been able to move on to bigger and better things.

“Looking back on what happened in 2011, it doesn’t seem as bad when you have four majors on your mantelpiece.”.

McIlroy’s contentment came with a caveat: it would be “unthinkable” if he did not win The Masters in his career.

Yet as he prepares for his 15th appearance at Augusta National this week, a green jacket remains an elusive missing item from his wardrobe.

Despite seven top-10 finishes in his past 10 Masters outings, the trophy remains the only thing separating McIlroy from joining the ranks of golf immortals to have completed golf’s career grand slam of all four majors in the modern era: Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, and Tiger Woods.

A runner-up finish to Scottie Scheffler last year marked McIlroy’s best finish at Augusta, yet arguably 2011 remains the closest he has ever been to victory. A slow start in 2022 meant McIlroy had begun Sunday’s deciding round 10 shots adrift of the American, who teed off for his final hole with a five-shot lead despite McIlroy’s brilliant 64 finish.

Rory McIlroy: I will win the Masters.

In a recent development, at 33 years old, time is still on his side. Though 2022 extended his major drought to eight years, it featured arguably his best golf since that golden season in 2014.

And as McIlroy knows better than most, things can change quickly at Augusta National.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 2026 National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) Championship final is upon us, with Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current set to battle it out for the title on November 21.
  • Washington booked their third consecutive final appearance with a victory over Utah Royals in the semi-finals, while Kansas City Current overcame reigning champions Gotham FC to move one step closer to lifting the trophy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2026 National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) Championship final is upon us, with Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current set to battle it out for the title on November 21.

Washington booked their third consecutive final appearance with a victory over Utah Royals in the semi-finals, while Kansas City Current overcame reigning champions Gotham FC to move one step closer to lifting the trophy.

With the two sides now preparing to meet at Audi Field in Washington, it is all to play for.

The 2026 NWSL playoffs began with eight teams battling for a place in the semi-finals, following a regular season in which Gotham FC emerged as the team to beat.

The defending champions finished top of the standings to claim the NWSL Shield for the first time and secure the No. 1 seed, while Washington Spirit, San Diego Wave, Kansas City Current, Angel City, Portland Thorns, Utah Royals and Seattle Reign also qualified.

The quarter-finals produced plenty of drama, with three of the four ties decided by a single goal.

Industry observers note that utah Royals pulled off the biggest upset, beating second seeds San Diego Wave 1-0 to secure their first-ever post-season victory. Kansas City Current also edged through, with Michelle Cooper converting an extra-time penalty to seal a 1-0 win over Angel City.

Gotham needed just one goal to overcome Seattle Reign, with an early own goal from Jordyn Bugg proving decisive.

According to recent reports, washington Spirit, meanwhile, delivered the standout performance of the round, sweeping aside Portland Thorns 4-1. Trinity Rodman scored twice, while Clara Luvanga contributed a goal and two assists.

The semi-finals then saw Washington continue their impressive form with a 2-1 victory over Utah, while Kansas City knocked out defending champions Gotham with the same scorline.

Now, just one game separates the two finalists from lifting the Championship trophy, with Washington Spirit looking to make home advantage count and Kansas City Current aiming to finish their campaign on the ultimate high.

Washington Spirit – Trinity Rodman.

According to recent reports, rodman has been central to Washington's success this season, recording a career-best 12 goals and eight assists in the regular season. The forward carried that form into the quarter-finals, scoring twice and providing an assist in the 4-1 victory over Portland. She backed this up with another assist as her side overcame Utah Royals in the semi-final. Named an NWSL MVP finalist, Rodman will be one of Washington's biggest attacking threats as they look to finally get over the line after consecutive Championship final defeats.

Kansas City Current – Croix Bethune.

Recent findings suggest that while Temwa Chawinga will often steal the headlines, Bethune has enjoyed an outstanding season since joining Kansas City from Washington, setting a new NWSL single-season record with 11 assists. The midfielder also made a major impact in the semi-finals, scoring a stunning free-kick to open the scoring in the 2-1 victory over Gotham. Her creativity and ability to unlock opposition defences will be crucial against her former club, particularly with two-time MVP Chawinga providing a constant attacking threat alongside her.

Prediction: Washington Spirit 1-2 Kansas City Current.

Washington, who were champions in 2021, will have the advantage of playing in front of their home supporters at Audi Field, but Kansas City Current have the attacking quality to spoil the occasion. Croix Bethune's creativity and Temwa Chawinga's threat in front of goal give them plenty of ways to hurt Spirit, while their semi-final victory over reigning champions Gotham will have given them a huge confidence boost.

Kansas City have unfinished business in the Championship after finishing runners-up to Portland Thorns in 2022. They have the opportunity to claim their first-ever NWSL Championship title, and with the quality throughout their squad, they could finally get their hands on the trophy. Washington will be determined to turn around their fortunes after heartbreak in back-to-back finals, but I fancy Kansas City to edge a memorable contest.

Chelsea must toughen up against Leeds – or risk being ‘bullied’ again

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • In a recent development, chelsea have a No 9 problem at both ends of the pitch.
  • According to recent reports, defeat at Sunderland brought accusations that Chelsea’s defence was susceptible to being “bullied”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

In a recent development, chelsea have a No 9 problem at both ends of the pitch. Up top, Xabi Alonso is struggling to find a solution in the absence of Joao Pedro, who has still not returned to training after weeks out with a thigh problem. And at the back, Alonso’s porous defence appears fallible in the face of the old-school striker’s revival.

According to recent reports, defeat at Sunderland brought accusations that Chelsea’s defence was susceptible to being “bullied”. The primary bully, in this case, was frontman Brian Brobbey, one of the Premier League’s most imposing units. His overpowering of Levi Colwill led to Sunderland’s controversial penalty that proved the difference two weeks ago.

Alonso didn’t agree with such a critique at the time. "Not bullied, I would say that it was a situation that we could have defended better,” he said after the match at the Stadium of Light. But amid Chelsea’s frantic form, questions are being asked whether Alonso’s back line can handle the Premier League at its most physical.

Sources indicate that in this regard, Saturday’s test of Leeds provides the ultimate test. There are few teams in the top-flight as physical as Leeds, even if Daniel Farke may sometimes opt to play down his players as “butterflies”, like he did for Jayden Bogle after the right-back avoided a red card for a challenge on Tottenham’s Mathys Tel.

In a recent development, leeds have won the most duels in the Premier League this season; Farke’s players are not scared of going in for a challenge. That has made them a particularly difficult team to score against, conceding a mere eight goals so far. Chelsea have let in double that tally, with only Arsenal and Brighton conceding fewer than the Whites.

Sources indicate that alonso isn’t only learning of English football’s physical requirement now; his five seasons at Liverpool would have taught him as such. And he knows that if his team continue to be beaten in this department, it will repeatedly cost them in this league regardless of the opposition. “It’s the Premier League. It’s not new,” Alonso stated. “It’s not just against Leeds. It will happen next week against Forest, and the next one against Palace. This is the level of the competition.”.

According to recent reports, ever the tactician, Alonso does not put full emphasis on brute physicality – even if it is a necessary step to unlocking quality. He continued: “It’s not just the duels – it’s about a football thing or tactical thing. When you have good control, normally you are in better positions to press and duel. When you don’t have that much control, you aren’t in that good position. It’s not just ‘one v one, let’s see what happens’. No, you can help situations to be stronger in duels. After, it’s the individual qualities that help.”.

It has been revealed that leeds nevertheless appeared to lean into the criticism in the build-up to their trip down south. They posted a compilation of their best moments against the Blues from over the years, which included its fair share of crunching tackles and Chelsea mistakes. Whether a statement of intent or merely mind games, Alonso said his side was only focusing on themselves. “We focus on not being soft tomorrow and being competitive,” he said. “That’s our goal.”.

Like Sunderland, Leeds’ main threat comes in the form of a traditional No 9. Dominic Calvert-Lewin may have been studying tape of Chelsea’s last outing and licking his lips this week, knowing that he has the capacity to cause the same sort of problems as Brobbey.

“We prepare knowing that we have prepared because it’s a player with different qualities but the same kind of profile,” Alonso said. “It’s nothing new. It’s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9.

In a recent development, “Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready for tomorrow.”.

Back in fashion, the target man profile is giving Chelsea’s young defence trouble. While Alonso’s arrival at Chelsea coincided with the move away from their chaos of youth, his back line remains fresh-faced. His five first-team centre-backs have an average age of 23, with Maxence Lacroix the oldest at 26. They all came into senior football with the old-school No 9 being just that, and the leap back in time has forced them to adapt.

According to recent reports, so far, the learning curve has been apparent. But Alonso doesn’t believe his players lack the tools to deal with what used to be the norm up top.

Sources indicate that asked if centre-backs have forgotten how to defend the traditional No 9, Alonso replied: “No, I don’t think forgotten. But it’s demanding to play against No 9s. They have good movement in the box, out the box. But this is the demand. You can ask the full-backs, they have to play against great wingers in one v one situations. But I don’t think it’s been forgotten.”.

In a recent development, alonso is personally happy to see the revival of the No 9. “It’s good they are back, these type of players,” he stated. Whether he still feels the same after the visit of Calvert-Lewin and the rest of Leeds’ hardmen may depend on his players toughening up to the task.

Breaking: ULA lost a Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying 40 Amazon satellites 10 minutes after launch — but the failure began just after liftoff

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (882 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space
